title: North Korea says it tested new torpedo system with AI capabilities
source_used: Associated Press (text read in The Hindu copy, same AP headline); cross-checked with Euronews
key_facts: North Korea said on Saturday 17 Oct 2026 that it had successfully tested a new torpedo system that uses AI for target detection and guidance.
North Korea's state news agency KCNA said the weapon, tested on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, is a 'super-speed, precisely guided' torpedo system named Zam-2.0.
KCNA did not explain what it meant by artificial intelligence.
The report said the test verified the weapon's propulsion systems, developed through more than 180 tests over five years.
South Korea's military, which often accuses the North of exaggerating its weapons, did not immediately comment.
The test follows North Korea's first underwater-launched missile tests in nearly three years on 14 Oct 2026, as Kim Jong Un shifts focus to naval capabilities.
Kim Yo Jong, Kim's sister, claimed missiles tested on 3 Oct 2026 also used AI; some experts doubt the weapons really have capabilities such as autonomous target designation.
quote_evidence: North Korea said on Saturday (October 17, 2026) it had successfully tested a new torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance.
It didn't explain what was meant by artificial intelligence.
South Korea's military, which often accuses the North of exaggerating its military technologies, did not immediately comment on KCNA's report.
why_it_matters_hint: A state-media claim of an AI-guided torpedo adds to North Korea's naval build-up, but the AI claim is unexplained and doubted by experts.
notes: AP original (apnews.com, HTTP 403) not opened; the text read in The Hindu carries the AP headline and style but the extracted page does not print an AP credit, so the match rests on the identical headline used by many US papers. The test date (15 Oct) is before 16 Oct but the claim first became public on 17 Oct, so freshness is NEW.
